$comment: Single source of truth for Field Guide box-category styling (colorClass + badge icon/name). Read by dm.html at runtime (fetched into SCC_FG_CATEGORY_STYLE) and by scripts/fg-template.mjs (check/build). Edit this file, not a hardcoded copy in either place — see CLAUDE.md Decision Log for the original SCC_FG_CATEGORY_STYLE object this was extracted from.

$specialCasedCategories.$comment: These box categories are NOT in `categories` above -- they never read colorClass/badge from this table at all, because sccFgRenderBlock() dispatches them to their own dedicated render function before the generic box case (which is the only consumer of `categories`) ever runs. Listed here so fg-template.mjs's `check` command knows they're recognized categories without treating their absence from `categories` as an unknown-category error. Do not add entries for these to `categories` -- that would imply they use the generic colorClass/badge box rendering, which they don't.
$specialCasedCategories.spoken_dialogue_note: spoken_dialogue IS also a real key in `categories` above (its own dedicated render function, sccFgRenderSpokenDialogue, reads categories.spoken_dialogue directly for its badge) -- it is not special-cased out of the table, just special-cased out of the *generic* box render path. Listed here only for cross-reference, not as an extra recognized-but-untabled category.
$specialCasedCategories.comedy_inline_note: comedy (with block.inline === true) is likewise a real key in `categories` -- sccFgRenderComedyInline() also reads categories.comedy for consistency, it just renders as a plain inline paragraph instead of a colored box shell. Not a separate category name.
$specialCasedCategories.quest_beats: Live, clickable quest-beat status widget (sccFgRenderQuestBeatsBlock). Ignores block.color/category styling entirely -- pulls its own content from SCC_SELECTED.quest + the quests table, not from any box color scheme.
$specialCasedCategories.combat_outcomes: Branching combat-outcome log widget (sccFgRenderCombatOutcomesBlock). Header now renders the real player_decision chip (see `categories` above) instead of a hardcoded icon+label, but the box shell itself still has its own fixed styling, no colorClass/badge lookup for the shell.
$specialCasedCategories.scenario_cards: Scenario Cards navigation module (sccFgRenderScenarioCardsBlock, 2026-08-26 rebuild) -- any-length array of cards, each with an optional entity portrait, rich block-array content (rendered via the same sccFgRenderDoc every other Field Guide content uses), and an optional decision selector (player_decision chip, click-to-log/unlog via the same shared session_note_entries mechanism combat_outcomes uses). Replaces the earlier scenario_tabs/approach_tracker categories entirely -- both are gone, not kept alongside this.
$specialCasedCategories.question_panel: Sticky Question Panel module (sccFgRenderQuestionPanelBlock, 2026-09-18) -- for a scene with several branching 'If Asked' questions where flat stacking makes one specific answered question hard to find again mid-session. Shape: { label (optional header subtitle), group_icons: {groupName: icon}, questions: [{id (required, stable), label, group, blocks: [...same shape as field_guide_sessions.blocks, rendered via sccFgRenderDoc]}] }. Left column is a sticky nav of question buttons grouped under their own group's icon (one icon per GROUP, not per question); each button carries its own Mark-Completed-style circle (independent of selecting the question), persisted via the same session_note_entries mechanism scenario_cards' status/decision state already uses. Completed questions sink to the bottom of their own group, never a global bottom.
$specialCasedCategories.scene_cast: Scene Cast quick-glance panel (sccFgRenderSceneCastBlock, 2026-09-18) -- a compact 'who matters right now' reference for a section with several NPCs active at once, placed as a normal box block right after the h2 it applies to. NOT a second NPC browser -- no search, no relationship/stat detail, just a portrait + name + one DM-authored state_note per cast member. Shape: { label (optional header subtitle), cast: [{entity_type (anything sccFgResolveFeaturedEntity resolves -- same vocabulary block.featured already uses: character/npc, creature, city/poi/nation, item, quest, organization, concept, pc), entity_id, state_note}] }. Portrait/name resolution reuses sccFgResolveFeaturedEntity() verbatim, the same function block.featured thumbnails use. Click opens the real lookup drawer (sccOpenLookup) for full detail -- skipped for entity_type 'pc', which has no lookup-drawer branch. Collapsible via a plain class toggle, session-only, not persisted.
$specialCasedCategories.guide_meta_note: guide_meta IS a real key in `categories` above (colorClass grey, badge null) but sccFgRenderBlock() returns '' for it unconditionally before the generic box case is ever reached -- confirmed intentionally unrendered (the old 'How to Use This Guide' box), not a bug. Data is kept, never displayed.

$recognizedLinkTypes.$comment: The type vocabulary an inline [[type:id|Label]] link actually resolves to when clicked. Fixed 2026-08-27 (QA round 4, item 8): sccOpenLookup() (dm.html) now resolves its `type` argument through the same SCC_FG_FEATURED_TYPE_ALIASES map block.featured entries already used (npc->character, poi/nation->city) before dispatching to its type-specific branches, so [[poi:...]]/[[npc:...]]/[[nation:...]] links resolve correctly now -- previously sccOpenLookup had no dedicated branch for those raw type strings, so a well-formed [[poi:...]] link opened the lookup drawer to a permanent 'No details available.' with no real error. `types` here lists every type an inline link's click target actually resolves to, aliases included -- kept as its own list rather than reused verbatim from SCC_FG_LINK_TYPES's keys, since an author should still be free to write [[city:...]] directly for a real city and either [[poi:...]] or [[city:...]] for a POI -- both are valid authoring choices now.

$railScope.$comment:
Single source of truth for whether/how a box category appears in the Field Guide jump rail (dm.html's sccFgCollectScrollEntries()). Added 2026-09-18 after question_panel shipped with ZERO rail integration -- it needed hand-wiring to show up at all, and nothing would have caught a future category making the same silent omission. scripts/fg-template.mjs's `check`/`build` commands now hard-error if ANY real box category (every key in `categories` above, plus every $specialCasedCategories key that isn't a cross-reference-only note) is missing from this object -- a new category literally cannot ship without a conscious rail decision. h1/h2 are NOT covered here: they're block TYPES, not box categories, and always get a rail entry unconditionally (see the collector's own h1/h2 handling, unchanged by this). One entry per category, shape: { "scope": "none" | "entry" | "container", ...scope-specific fields below }.

`scope: "none"` -- never appears in the rail, regardless of whether the block has a real block.label. This is the right default for leaf content boxes (Read Aloud, DM Only, Spoken Dialogue, etc.) -- a real check against Session 1/2 content found 30-33 labeled DM Only/Read Aloud boxes per session alone; surfacing every labeled box would flood the rail past usefulness. These are supplementary content WITHIN a scene, not scene boundaries themselves.

`scope: "entry"` -- gets exactly one rail entry. `labelField` names the block field holding its display text (required real content, schema-checked already for combat_outcomes). `tier` (default "h2" if omitted) sets which visual tier (dot/label size) it renders at -- see .scc-fg-scroll-dot--h1/h2/sub in dm.html's CSS.

`scope: "container"` -- the category owns an array of its own navigable, individually-labeled sub-items (cards, questions, etc.) that the collector recurses into for real, generic 'at any nesting level' support. `childrenField` names the block field holding that array; `childLabelField` names each child's own label field; each child gets a tier:"card" rail entry. `hasOwnEntry` (bool) additionally controls whether the CONTAINER ITSELF also gets a top-level entry (using `labelField`/`entryFallbackLabel` the same way scope:"entry" does) before its children -- scenario_cards keeps its long-standing hasOwnEntry:false (it's conventionally preceded by a real h1/h2 that already serves as its landmark; adding a redundant second entry right on top of it was never the ask and would be a visible regression), while question_panel is hasOwnEntry:true since it commonly has no heading of its own and is exactly the case that motivated this whole change -- the DM sees 'Common Questions' in the rail now, not just its individual questions once the section happens to already be visible. A container category's own render function is responsible for tagging each child's clickable tile/button element with data-fg-rail-child-label="<text>" (see sccFgOneScenarioCardsHtml/sccFgOneQuestionPanelHtml in dm.html) -- that shared attribute, not a category name, is what the collector actually queries for, so a brand-new container-shaped category gets full recursive rail support (including children) the moment it (a) declares itself here and (b) tags its own children with that one attribute -- no dm.html collector edit required either way.

quest_beats.$why: A live, per-session quest-progress status widget, not itself a distinct authored scene -- the quest it displays already has its own navigation elsewhere. Unchanged from today's behavior.

combat_outcomes.$why: block.label is already required content (widget header + log-entry title prefix) -- a real, DM-authored 'moment' name, e.g. a specific fight's branching outcomes. Its own outcomes[] are short inline options within ONE widget, not separate navigable scenes, so they don't become child rail entries the way scenario_cards' cards or question_panel's questions do.
